diagnostic_approaches.name: Intelligent Nasopharyngoscope Localization Monitoring Assistant (ILMA)

diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: achieving a classification accuracy of 97.60% through the process of training and validation utilizing endoscopic images.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nakajo et al. pharyngeal/laryngeal anatomical site classifier with blind spot identification
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify pharyngeal and laryngeal anatomical sites and identify blind spots

diagnostic_approaches.name: Ren et al. 2020 CNN-based vocal cord lesion classifier
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify vocal cord nodules, polyps, leukoplakia, and malignant tumors
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: CNN trained on laryngoscopic images using hue, texture, and geometry features
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Recognizes lesion categories with reported per-class accuracies
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: For automated classification of vocal cord lesions on images
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: reached recognition accuracies of 98% for vocal cord nodules, 91% for polyps, 91% for leukoplakia, and 90% for malignant tumors

diagnostic_approaches.name: Kuo et al. 2021 AI-assisted diagnostic system for laryngeal lesions
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Objective detection and classification of laryngeal lesions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Selects clear images, segments vocal cords, and performs quantitative hue/geometric analysis
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Provides automated classification of healthy, leukoplakia, polyps, cysts, and tumors
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Analysis of laryngoscope video images
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: It achieved a classification accuracy of 100% for healthy vocal cords and leukoplakia and 93.15%, 95.16%, and 96.42% accuracy for polyps, cysts, and tumor lesions, respectively.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Zhao et al. 2022 DCNN-based vocal cord lesion diagnostic system
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Distinguish normal, polyps, keratosis, and cancer; urgent vs nonurgent classification
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: DCNN analyzes laryngoscopic images for lesion categorization
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Outputs lesion type; also classifies urgency
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Automated analysis of vocal cord lesions on images/videos
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The overall accuracy of this system was 80.23%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Chen et al. 2023 3D VOSNet for vocal cord/glottis segmentation
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Segment vocal cords and glottis; compute objective quantitative parameters
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Applies 3D VOSNet to video laryngoscopy for segmentation and parameter computation
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Quantitative parameters assist diagnosis (e.g., vocal cord paralysis)
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Objective assessment of vocal cord conditions on video laryngoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: computed six parameters that include the glottal area, vocal cord area, vocal cord length, vocal cord length deviation, and vocal cord symmetry.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Xiong et al. 2019 DL model for laryngeal cancer/precancer detection
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assist in recognizing laryngeal cancer and precancerous lesions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: DL model trained on laryngoscopic images
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Provides diagnostic output with reported accuracy and sensitivity
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Early diagnosis support in laryngoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: achieving an accuracy of 86.7% and a sensitivity of 73.1% in recognizing laryngeal cancer and precancerous lesions.

diagnostic_approaches.name: DL models for pharyngeal cancer using WLI/NBI/BLI (Atsuko 2020; Mitsuhiro 2021)

diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Model outputs cancer recognition with stated accuracies
limitations: number of patient cases included was relatively small
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Analysis of upper GI endoscopic images for pharyngeal cancer
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: These models achieved recognition accuracies of 100% and 92%, although the number of patient cases included in the validation assessment was relatively small

diagnostic_approaches.name: Laryngopharyngeal AI Diagnostic System (LPAIDS) 2023

diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Reported high accuracy and sensitivity ranges
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Real-time laryngoscopy analysis for laryngopharyngeal cancer
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: impressive accuracy (0.949–0.984) and sensitivity (0.901–0.986).

diagnostic_approaches.name: SegMENT-Plus (Sampieri et al. 2024) for laryngeal cancer boundary delineation

diagnostic_approaches.name: Paderno et al. 2021 fully CNN tumor segmentation (oral/oropharyngeal)

diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: automatically segmented tumors with Dice similarity coefficients (DSC) of 0.6559 and 0.7603

diagnostic_approaches.name: Girdler et al. 2021 CNN for nasal polyps vs inverted papilloma

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopic examination time-lapse assessment (quality criterion)

diagnostic_approaches.name: NPL patient maneuvers per region (exposure technique)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Optimize exposure of specific NPL regions for examination
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Nasal breathing (nasopharynx); tongue extension (epiglottis); inhalation/phonation (vocal cord); phonation/air inflation (piriform fossa)
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Improved exposure reduces missed diagnoses
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During NPL to expose target anatomical areas

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Improve exposure of entire hypopharynx

diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Enhances visualization to prevent missed diagnoses
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When hypopharyngeal exposure is unsatisfactory
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Better exposure of the entire hypopharynx can be achieved through head rotation, the Valsalva maneuver, and the Killian position.

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess the image quality and decide whether to discard low-quality images

diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: discard the image if it is below a certain quality threshold
limitations: mistakes in the recognition of bronchial parts or detection of lesions could happen
leading to a less reliable bronchoscopic AI system.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopic branch recognition for quality control (31-class classification)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Determine which bronchial site/part the current bronchoscopic image covers for quality control

diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: AI-assisted is indeed possible.
limitations: a level higher than the third level is hard to implement
since not only is such a bronchoscope very expensive but also it is hard for a bronchoscopist to operate.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: bronchoscopic quality control

diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Lesions are localized by bounding boxes with category labels.
limitations: mistakes in the recognition of bronchial parts or detection of lesions could happen
leading to a less reliable bronchoscopic AI system.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Single-stage detection methods (e.g., SSD, RetinaNet, YOLO)

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Object detection model
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: transformer-based models have also been introduced for object detection, such as the DETR (Detection Transformer) model, which marks a new development direction

diagnostic_approaches.name: YOLOX (You Only Look Once) for lesion detection
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Lesion detection (bronchoscopic/endoscopic images)
criteria_or_scoring: Category prediction loss (BCE with logits loss)
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: YOLOX comprises input, backbone (CSP-DarkNet), neck (FPN, PAN), and predictor with Decoupled Head; an IoU branch is added to the regression branch.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Example: normal bronchus (no detection box); benign lesion (blue box); malignant lesion (red box).
limitations: Single-stage methods may be slightly less accurate than two-stage methods.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: This book chapter demonstrates how to utilize the YOLO model (more specifically, YOLO X) for the task of lesion detection.
